facts.text: Liquidity is cash of USD 280 million, about 58% of it outside the U.S., plus an undrawn USD 350 million asset-based revolver due November 2029, more than twelve months away. Availability under that revolver depends on a borrowing base and letters of credit that are not disclosed, so undrawn capacity is a ceiling, not a measure, and no debt matures before 2029. The term loan and secured notes carry no financial maintenance covenants, only negative covenants, and the revolver's covenants are not described, so covenant headroom is not established. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that behaviour since closing has been creditor-friendly: the company repaid USD 65 million of debt in nine months, shows no distribution after the closing payment, described the third quarter as a record with Adjusted EBITDA of USD 99 million and kept its free cash flow outlook. The auditor's opinion on the financial statements themselves was unqualified and the largest customer is only about 14% of sales. The view would turn more positive if remediation removed the control weaknesses and the proxy statement showed dispersed holders with no fee arrangements. It would turn more negative if a holder with consent rights emerged, if an acquisition were funded with debt, or if debt repayment stopped while restructuring spend continued. Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so holders above any threshold, board independence, committee roles, executive pay and any fees to holders are not established. Severity High. The 2026 proxy statement would close it. - No executed indenture, term loan agreement or revolver agreement was supplied, so the capacity to pay distributions, make investments or incur debt is not established, and behaviour cannot be separated from legal capacity. Severity High. The executed documents would close it. - The terms of the services, tax matters and employee matters agreements with the former parent are not stated, so the cost and duration of the legacy IT dependency are not established. Severity Medium. - Revolver availability, letters of credit, covenants and compliance certificates are not stated. Severity Medium. A compliance certificate would close it. - Customer names, contract tenors and renewal dates are not disclosed, so revenue durability is not established beyond the share of sales held by the largest customers. Severity Medium. - No result after the quarter ended June 27, 2026 is supplied, so later repayment, margin and control remediation are not established. Severity Medium. The fiscal 2026 annual report would close it. - Synergy and cost-saving figures are management estimates and their realisation status is not stated. Severity Medium. - No sponsor is named in the run settings or the documents, so fund vintage, sponsor economics and sponsor equity contribution do not apply and are not assessed. Severity Low. - The source for the difference between the face amount of closing debt and the cash proceeds is not supplied. Severity Low.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. First, there is no debt maturity before October 2029 and no financial maintenance covenant on the term loan and secured notes, so default before 2029 would need a sharp earnings fall rather than a covenant trip. Second, liquidity of USD 630 million, cash plus the undrawn revolver, equals 33.14% of debt and is the main cushion against a near-term cash shortfall. Third, deleveraging is under way: debt repayments of USD 65 million and trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million lowered adjusted leverage from 5.51x to 5.11x. Fourth, the business spans two regions, 45 plants and more than 1,000 customers, so no single plant or region carries the whole credit. Fifth, the price-cost spread turned positive by USD 11 million in the third quarter, showing that pass-through can work. facts.text: Magnera is a listed company created on November 4, 2024 when Treasure Holdco, a Berry subsidiary, merged with Glatfelter; pre-merger Treasure holders received 90% and Glatfelter holders kept 10%. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Reported sales move with raw-material prices more than with volume, so sales are not a margin measure. In the first nine months of fiscal 2026 net sales rose 3.38% to USD 2,445 million, helped by USD 105 million of foreign currency and USD 112 million of merger revenue, and held back by a USD 117 million cut in selling prices and a 1% organic volume decline. In the third quarter volume turned positive at 1% and sales rose 2.15%. Pricing power is limited: costs pass through contractually only over time, at renewals and by other means, and customers can switch suppliers. Revenue is therefore recurring in demand, concentrated in buyers, cyclical in price and exposed to share loss to competitors including Ahlstrom, Avgol, Mativ, PFNonwovens, Freudenberg and Fitesa. In the first nine months of fiscal 2026 net sales rose 3.38% to USD 2,445 million, helped by USD 105 million of foreign currency and USD 112 million of merger revenue, and held back by a USD 117 million cut in selling prices and a 1% organic volume decline. In the third quarter volume turned positive at 1% and sales rose 2.15%. Pricing power is limited: costs pass through contractually only over time, at renewals and by other means, and customers can switch suppliers. Revenue is therefore recurring in demand, concentrated in buyers, cyclical in price and exposed to share loss to competitors including Ahlstrom, Avgol, Mativ, PFNonwovens, Freudenberg and Fitesa.

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Cost of goods sold was 89.48% of fiscal 2025 net sales, leaving a gross margin of 10.52%, and selling, general and administrative cost 5.93%, so each 1% of net sales lost to unrecovered cost removes USD 33 million, about 8.83% of trailing adjusted EBITDA. The gross margin improved to 13.07% in the third quarter as the price-cost spread gained USD 11 million, helped by Project CORE and merger synergies. Raw materials are polymer resin, wood-based fibers and pulps, and energy and labour inflation also matter, but the fixed and variable cost split is not disclosed, so operating leverage cannot be measured. Margins can be defended only while pass-through works, which it did not in the Americas in fiscal 2025 when the price-cost spread cost USD 14 million. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is high because named competitors include Ahlstrom, Avgol, Mativ, PFNonwovens, Freudenberg and Fitesa and competition is on price, service, quality and delivery, so unrecovered cost cannot be passed on easily and margin is exposed. Buyer power is high because the top ten customers hold about 42% of sales and many have no long-term arrangement, so volume and price are renegotiated at renewal and earnings can step down. Supplier power is moderate to high because resin and pulp prices are set outside the company and pass through with a lag, which makes cash conversion volatile. The threat of new entrants is moderate because plants, technology and customer qualification need capital, and the threat of substitutes is not established by the documents read. facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Tariffs, inflation and currency are material enough to affect cash flow. Management cites changing tariffs and sanctions, inflation and market softness in its outlook. Sales are 43.63% in the United States and Canada and 56.37% elsewhere, and translation exposure to the euro, British pound, Argentine peso and Brazilian real moves reported sales and debt service, partly hedged by cross-currency swaps. The credit consequence is volatility in reported leverage and a pass-through test for tariffs, not a separate default driver. facts.text: Strengths are the 2029 maturity floor, USD 630 million of liquidity, falling adjusted leverage and regional diversification; weaknesses are thin cover, low cash conversion, the reported-to-adjusted gap and customer concentration. Opportunities that could raise credit quality are full delivery of Project CORE and merger savings, a fourth quarter that meets the free cash flow outlook, and remediation of the control weaknesses. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: For the next twelve to twenty-four months the issuer's fiscal 2026 outlook is Adjusted EBITDA at the lower end of its range of USD 380 million to USD 410 million, operating cash flow of USD 150 million to USD 170 million, capital spending of USD 60 million and free cash flow of USD 90 million to USD 110 million. With nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 282 million the low end implies USD 98 million in the fourth quarter, level with the third quarter, and the free cash flow range implies USD 58 million to USD 78 million, which is a large step from a third-quarter outflow of USD 28 million. Tailwinds are the price-cost spread gain, a 1% organic volume gain in the third quarter, currency translation and Project CORE; headwinds are weak European volume, tariffs, raw-material inflation that management called a significant spike, restructuring cash and interest cost. Over three to five years the 2029 and 2031 maturities, the euro swap maturities in November 2027 and November 2029, and thin goodwill cushions of 6.71% and 7.88% at the last test dominate; an impairment would be non-cash but would signal weaker expected earnings. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts with a raw-material cost spike that is passed on late while European volume stays soft, as in fiscal 2025 when organic volume fell 2% and the Americas price-cost spread cost USD 14 million. The first operating break is a negative price-cost spread, which cuts adjusted EBITDA; an illustrative case uses the lowest reported quarter, USD 84 million, annualised to USD 336 million, USD 36 million or 9.68% below the trailing figure; that quarter included Glatfelter only from November 4, 2024, so the case is harsher than a like-for-like trough. Debt of USD 1,901 million would be 5.66x that EBITDA and cash interest of USD 124 million would take 36.90% of it, and free cash flow would fall from USD 113 million to about USD 77 million before any tax effect. Management levers are cutting capital spending, which already fell by USD 20 million, ending restructuring spend and stopping prepayments; liquidity of USD 630 million and the absence of maturities before 2029 mean resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis in the window, but refinancing the 2029 notes at that earnings level would be harder and costlier. The observable triggers are a negative price-cost spread, organic volume turning negative again and a fourth-quarter free cash flow below USD 58 million. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Magnera presents an average business profile supported by regional and end-market diversification, 45 plants and no debt maturity before 2029, but credit quality is constrained by thin cash cover, the USD 122 million gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA, customer concentration and a weak control environment. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was USD 32 million in nine months and negative in the third quarter. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth and market access for USD 1,966 million of principal due in 2029 and 2031. The primary downside path is a raw-material cost spike passed on late, cutting adjusted EBITDA toward the lowest quarterly run-rate. Further analysis would require revolver availability, interim cash interest, receivable-program balances, the proxy statement and the executed debt documents. Top risk: thin cash cover on a debt load that must be refinanced in 2029 and 2031. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C05; calculation C08

- Revolver availability net of letters of credit and any borrowing-base limit is not stated, so liquidity of USD 630 million is a ceiling and not a measure. Severity High. A compliance certificate would close it. - Cash interest paid is disclosed only for fiscal 2025, so interest cover cannot be trended on a cash basis. Severity High. The next annual report would close it. - No result after the quarter ended June 27, 2026 is supplied, so whether the free cash flow outlook was met is not established. Severity High. The fiscal 2026 annual report would close it. - The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA and the 7.60x multiple rest on a calculated definition. Severity Medium. - No ratings, market prices or peer figures are supplied, so refinancing capacity and relative position are judged from the filings only. Severity Medium. - The proxy statement and executed debt documents are not supplied, so ownership, consent rights, restricted-payment capacity and covenant terms of the revolver are not established. Severity Medium. - Amounts sold under receivable programs are not disclosed, so cash conversion may be flattered by an unknown amount. Severity Medium. - The fixed and variable split of costs and the size of Project CORE savings are not disclosed, so operating leverage and savings delivery cannot be measured. Severity Low. - Customer names, contract tenor and market share are not disclosed. Severity Low. - The illustrative downside uses the lowest reported quarter and is arithmetic, not a forecast; no scenario assumptions were supplied. Severity Low.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Readiness is partial: the seven supplied filings and releases support a credit snapshot of Magnera Corporation through the June 2026 quarter, but creditors cannot test covenants, security or ratings because no debt documents, ratings or market prices were supplied. The financial inputs are internally consistent: the debt table reconciles to USD 1,901 million of carrying value, and issuer-stated trailing twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million reconciles to the annual and year-to-date figures.

The evidence stops at the quarter ended June 27, 2026, 131 days before the as-of date, so the fiscal fourth quarter that ended on September 26, 2026 is not covered. Revolver availability cannot be measured because letters of credit and the borrowing base are not stated, and the amounts sold under customer receivable programs are not disclosed.

spans.text: ## Request

Financial foundation for Magnera Corp (issuer magn) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the fiscal 2025 annual statements, the three fiscal 2026 quarterly statements, carrying-value debt, liquidity, trailing twelve-month leverage and coverage, and separately identified subsequent events.
## Sources

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Magnera is thinly covered but slowly deleveraging: debt is 5.11x trailing adjusted EBITDA at June 27, 2026 against 5.51x at the fiscal 2025 year end, yet 7.60x on reported EBITDA, so creditors should underwrite on cash generation, not on adjusted earnings. Net debt fell by only USD 26 million over three quarters, from USD 1,647 million to USD 1,621 million, while nine-month free cash flow was only USD 32 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C13

Cash interest of USD 124 million absorbed 35.03% of fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA, the full-year free cash flow outlook of USD 90 million to USD 110 million needs a fourth quarter far stronger than the third, and all USD 1,966 million of principal falls due in 2029 and 2031.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C05; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12
### Analysis by dimension

Leverage is falling because debt is being repaid, not because earnings are rising fast. Principal fell by USD 65 million between the fiscal 2025 year end and June 27, 2026, equal to the nine-month repayments, while trailing adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 354 million to USD 372 million. The same debt is 7.60x trailing reported EBITDA of USD 250 million, because USD 122 million of add-backs separate reported from adjusted EBITDA, namely restructuring, business optimization and other charges and non-cash items that the issuer does not count as ongoing operations. If those charges persist, the adjusted multiple overstates debt capacity and creditors are closer to the reported multiple.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07

Coverage is the thinnest point of the credit. Net interest expense was USD 112 million over nine months against adjusted EBITDA of USD 282 million, and the only reported cash interest figure, USD 124 million for fiscal 2025, gives adjusted cover of 2.85x and reported cover of 1.70x. The floating-rate term loan prices at 4.25% over SOFR, so a 0.25% rate move changes annual interest by about USD 2 million; interim cash interest is not disclosed, so interim cover is not calculable.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19

Cash-flow quality is weak relative to the earnings reported. Fiscal 2025 operating cash flow of USD 103 million less capital expenditure of USD 67 million is USD 36 million, not the USD 126 million the issuer prints, because the issuer adds USD 90 million of pre-merger cash flow. In the nine months to June 2026 operating cash flow was USD 76 million and free cash flow USD 32 million, and the third quarter alone used USD 13 million of operating cash, so the outlook of USD 90 million to USD 110 million for the year depends on a fourth quarter of USD 58 million to USD 78 million. The issuer lowered its operating cash flow outlook to USD 150 million to USD 170 million while keeping the free cash flow range by cutting planned capital spending to USD 60 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-03-28_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12

Liquidity is cash of USD 280 million, about 58% of it outside the U.S., plus an undrawn USD 350 million asset-based revolver due November 2029, more than twelve months away. Availability under that revolver depends on a borrowing base and letters of credit that are not disclosed, so undrawn capacity is a ceiling, not a measure, and no debt matures before 2029. The term loan and secured notes carry no financial maintenance covenants, only negative covenants, and the revolver's covenants are not described, so covenant headroom is not established. The refinancing risk is therefore later and larger: USD 500 million in 2029 and USD 1,466 million in 2031 on a business that generated USD 32 million of free cash flow in nine months.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C05

Debt repayment is slowing as cash generation weakens: the issuer repaid USD 27 million in the first quarter and USD 36 million in the second, but only USD 2 million in the third. Outside the debt figure, creditors also face operating lease liabilities of USD 60 million, a USD 78 million cross-currency swap liability, an unfunded USD 27 million pension obligation, an environmental liability of USD 17 million and Brazilian tax claims that may reach USD 66 million, and the size of customer receivable programs is not disclosed.

Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-03-28_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ef20072634_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C15

Data quality limits how far these figures can be pushed. Internal control over financial reporting was not effective at the fiscal 2025 year end and disclosure controls were not effective at June 27, 2026, the fiscal 2024 comparatives are carve-out statements with no debt, and amounts sold under customer receivable programs are not disclosed, so working capital and operating cash flow may be flattered by an unknown amount.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27

No subsequent event after the latest balance-sheet date changes net debt in the documents read, and no fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 figure is supplied, so every balance and ratio is as at June 27, 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 21

## Gaps

- Fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 results are not supplied: the fiscal year ended on September 26, 2026, before the as-of date, so every balance and trailing ratio is as at June 27, 2026 and year-end net debt and leverage cannot be stated. Severity High. The fiscal 2026 annual report would close it.

- Cash interest paid is not disclosed for any interim period or for fiscal 2024, so interim interest cover is not calculable and the one cover figure rests on fiscal 2025, a year that includes pre-merger months. Severity High. The next annual report's cash interest note would close it.

- Revolver borrowing base, availability and letters of credit are not stated, so undrawn capacity of USD 350 million is the commitment less nil borrowings and not a measure of available liquidity. Severity Medium. A borrowing-base certificate would close it.

- Amounts sold under customer receivable programs are not disclosed, so working capital and operating cash flow cannot be adjusted for receivables sold without recourse. Severity Medium. Disclosure of program balances would close it.

- The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated from operating income and depreciation and amortization and excludes other expense, net, which was USD 30 million in fiscal 2025 and included a USD 15 million debt prepayment charge. Severity Medium.

- No source states the legal rank, collateral or guarantor scope of the term loan, the revolver or the two secured notes, so the debt stack is not established and all four instruments have no ranking in the instrument register. Severity Medium. The indentures and credit agreements would close it.

- Carrying value is not disclosed by instrument, so the instrument register shows principal in the reporting-currency column and one financing cost adjustment of USD 65 million, and no interest-rate floor is stated for the floating-rate facilities. Severity Low.

- Operating indicators that the issuer states only annually or only for some periods, such as customer concentration and the consolidated price-cost spread effect, are shown as not supplied in the periods that do not print them. Severity Low.

- The balance sheet and debt note print a dash for long-term debt at September 28, 2024, so total debt for fiscal 2024 is carried as not supplied rather than zero, although liabilities and equity sum without any debt. Severity Low.

- Lines printed as a dash in a filing, and lines printed in one filing format only (the annual cash flow working-capital detail and the quarterly working-capital totals, the corporate expense allocation and goodwill impairment lines, and the pre-merger parent investment), are carried as not supplied in the periods that do not print them. Severity Low.
- Discrete second-quarter and third-quarter cash flows are not printed; the third-quarter operating cash flow of USD -13 million is derived from nine-month and six-month figures. Severity Low.

- The fiscal 2024 comparatives are carve-out statements of the Berry business with no debt, and fiscal 2025 includes Glatfelter only from November 4, 2024, so growth and leverage across the merger are not like for like. Severity Medium.

- Segment total assets and capital expenditure are not disclosed because the chief operating decision maker does not use them, and capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth. Severity Low.

- Internal control over financial reporting was not effective at the fiscal 2025 year end and disclosure controls were not effective at June 27, 2026; management states no material error resulted. Severity Medium.

Business and governance fact pack for Magnera Corp (issuer magn) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, the November 2024 merger and financing, ownership and control, operating drivers, capital allocation and governance, from the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases.
## Sources

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Magnera's creditor risk is a debt-funded separation and weak controls, not a sponsor: no controlling holder is disclosed, but USD 1,111 million went to the former parent at closing and internal controls are not effective.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 20

The business is diversified by region and end market but concentrated by customer, with the top ten customers about 42% of net sales, and its thin segment margins depend on passing resin and pulp costs through to customers with a lag; the latest year shows self-help gains but also USD 61 million of restructuring cost in nine months.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 7
### Key findings

- Ownership and control are undisclosed rather than benign. The 10-K says the pre-merger Treasure shareholders received 90% of the combined company and the Glatfelter shareholders kept 10%, but names no holder, board seat, consent right or fee, because those items sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. There is no sponsor in the run settings, so the creditor question is whether any holder can steer financial policy, and the documents read cannot answer it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 44; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The capital structure was built for the separation, not for the operating business. The new term loan and the 7.25% secured notes raised USD 1,556 million of cash proceeds, USD 1,111 million of which went to the former parent as a cash distribution (71.40% of the proceeds), and the filing says the remainder helped retire part of Glatfelter's debt. Creditors therefore carry interest on borrowing whose main use was a payment to a holder that no longer controls the company.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C02

- Customer concentration and the lag in cost pass-through are the main business risks. The top customer is about 14% and the top ten customers about 42% of net sales, many customers have no long-term arrangement, and resin and pulp costs are passed on only over time. In fiscal 2025 organic volume fell by 2% and the price-cost spread cost the Americas segment USD 14 million of Adjusted EBITDA, so a raw-material spike or a customer switch hits earnings before prices catch up.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27

- Margins are improving through self-help that costs cash. Restructuring and other activities charges were USD 89 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 61 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, equal to 25.14% and 21.63% of Adjusted EBITDA, while the third-quarter price-cost spread added USD 11 million. The synergies the issuer cites are management estimates, so creditors should treat them as unrealised until cash flow shows them.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C05

- Governance is the clearest creditor-adverse area. Internal control over financial reporting was not effective at the fiscal 2025 year end, the auditor gave an adverse opinion on it, disclosure controls were still not effective at June 27, 2026, and legacy U.S. systems run under a transition services agreement with the former parent. Management reports no material error, so the effect is lower confidence in the numbers and slower detection of problems, not a known misstatement.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 20

- Capital allocation since closing has favoured creditors, but the stated appetite for acquisitions could reverse that. The cash flow statements show debt repayments of USD 65 million in nine months and no dividend or buyback line, while the third-quarter report says the company intends to pursue further acquisitions. A debt-funded purchase would raise leverage that is only slowly falling.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 14

- Sponsor and governance risk is Medium. Documented behaviour is mixed, the control environment is weak and ownership is not disclosed, but there is no recorded dividend recapitalisation, creditor-adverse amendment or exchange since closing.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 43
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that behaviour since closing has been creditor-friendly: the company repaid USD 65 million of debt in nine months, shows no distribution after the closing payment, described the third quarter as a record with Adjusted EBITDA of USD 99 million and kept its free cash flow outlook. The auditor's opinion on the financial statements themselves was unqualified and the largest customer is only about 14% of sales. The view would turn more positive if remediation removed the control weaknesses and the proxy statement showed dispersed holders with no fee arrangements. It would turn more negative if a holder with consent rights emerged, if an acquisition were funded with debt, or if debt repayment stopped while restructuring spend continued.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27
### Limitations
- The proxy statement was not supplied, so the finding that no controlling holder is disclosed could change if a holder with board or consent rights exists; sponsor-style risks would then apply.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 45

- No indenture or credit agreement was supplied, so restricted-payment, investment and acquisition capacity is not assessed and the capital-allocation view rests on behaviour alone; a permissive document would weaken the favourable reading.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47

- The evidence ends with the June 2026 quarter, so the repayment trend, which slowed to USD 2 million in the third quarter, may have moved further; a stop in repayment would move the capital-allocation finding from favourable to mixed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-03-28_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Synergy and cost-saving figures are management estimates and customer names and contract terms are not disclosed, so the concentration and self-help findings are stated as shares and charges, not as durable earnings.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27

| Product lines | Personal Care 48% and Consumer Solutions 52% of fiscal 2025 net sales; 45% and 55% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 | Mix is shifting toward consumer solutions, which management links to volume strength | 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 11 |

| Customers | Top customer about 14% and top ten customers about 42% of fiscal 2025 net sales; many customers have no long-term arrangement | Concentration plus short contracts makes volume and price negotiable at renewal | 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27 |

| Raw materials and pricing | Polymer resin, wood-based fibers and pulps; cost changes are passed through contractual mechanisms over time, at renewals and by other means | The lag between cost and price swings margin and cash conversion | 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8 |

| Competition | Competitors named include Ahlstrom, Avgol, Mativ, PFNonwovens, Freudenberg and Fitesa; competition is on price, service, quality and delivery | Larger or better-funded rivals can undercut price in a downturn | 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8 |

| Cost programme | Project CORE capacity rationalisations announced in fiscal 2025, expected over two years at about USD 20 million of cost in the annual report outlook | Savings are meant to offset softness, but restructuring charges to date are far above the original estimate | 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 40 |

### Company profile
| Item | Detail | Source |

| Listing and shares | Common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange as MAGN; 35.8 million shares outstanding on 2026-08-06 | 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 1 |
| Headquarters | Charlotte, North Carolina, United States | 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 1 |

| Employees | About 8,500 in the annual report; 8,000 or more in the third-quarter release | 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2 |

| Customers | More than 1,000 customers per the release; top ten about 42% of fiscal 2025 net sales | EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27 |

| Auditor | Ernst & Young LLP, auditor since 2024; unqualified opinion on the financial statements and adverse opinion on internal control | 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 22 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On November 4, 2024 Treasure Holdco, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Berry Global Group, Inc., merged with Glatfelter Corporation, which was renamed Magnera Corporation. Treasure shareholders received 90% of the combined company and Glatfelter shareholders kept 10%, and Treasure was the accounting acquirer, so the fiscal 2024 figures are carve-out statements of the business Berry contributed. Total consideration was the USD 74 million fair value of Glatfelter common stock, and Glatfelter debt with a fair value of USD 869 million was assumed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 32

To fund the closing the company put in place a USD 785 million term loan due 2031, a USD 800 million issue of 7.25% First Priority Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and a USD 350 million asset-based revolver due 2029, and it kept Glatfelter's 4.75% notes due 2029. The statement of cash flows shows proceeds from long-term borrowings of USD 1,556 million, a cash distribution to Berry of USD 1,111 million and repayments of USD 484 million; the filing says the term loan and 7.25% note proceeds retired part of Glatfelter's debt and funded the distribution. The face amounts of USD 785 million and USD 800 million add to USD 1,585 million, USD 29 million more than the cash proceeds shown, and no source explains the difference.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C01

The fiscal 2026 cash flow statements show no proceeds from borrowings. Outstanding principal has been reduced by prepayments, to USD 706 million on the term loan and USD 760 million on the 7.25% notes at June 27, 2026, while the revolver is undrawn. No acquisition, sponsor transaction or refinancing after the merger is described, and the third-quarter report says only that the company intends to pursue acquisition targets.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Magnera Corp (issuer magn) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the credit view built from Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance, tested against the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases.
## Sources

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Magnera is a thinly covered, slowly deleveraging credit with no maturity before 2029 and workable liquidity, so creditors face limited near-term default risk but a refinancing that depends on cash generation the company has not yet shown.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C07

Debt is 5.11x trailing adjusted EBITDA but 7.60x on reported EBITDA, adjusted cash interest cover was 2.85x in fiscal 2025, and nine-month free cash flow of USD 32 million sits against an outlook of USD 90 million to USD 110 million. Liquidity of USD 630 million is the main cushion, though how much of it is available is not measured.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C07
### Key findings

- Leverage is moderate on the issuer's measure and high on the reported one. Total debt is 5.11x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million, down from 5.51x at the fiscal 2025 year end, and 7.60x trailing reported EBITDA of USD 250 million. The USD 122 million gap between them is restructuring, optimisation and non-cash add-backs, so the adjusted multiple is credible only if those charges stop recurring.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04

- Interest cover and cash conversion are the weakest dimensions. Net cash interest of USD 124 million took 35.03% of fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA, with reported cover at 1.70x, and free cash flow after capital spending was USD 113 million over the trailing twelve months against adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million. Little cash is therefore left for debt reduction, so deleveraging depends on earnings growth more than on repayment.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C05; calculation C06

- Near-term liquidity and the maturity profile are the strongest support. Cash of USD 280 million plus an undrawn USD 350 million revolver gives USD 630 million, equal to 33.14% of debt, no debt matures before October 2029, and the term loan and secured notes have no financial maintenance covenants. Default before 2029 would need a sharp earnings fall, but availability under the revolver is not measured and 58% of cash is outside the U.S.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C07

- The earnings base is improving, partly through self-help and with concentrated customers. Adjusted EBITDA rose 8.79% in the third quarter on a USD 11 million price-cost gain, and trailing adjusted EBITDA is USD 18 million above fiscal 2025, but restructuring charges were USD 61 million in nine months and the top ten customers hold about 42% of sales without long-term arrangements.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C08

- Control weaknesses and undisclosed ownership limit confidence in the figures. Internal control over financial reporting was not effective at the fiscal 2025 year end and disclosure controls were not effective at June 27, 2026, and no current holder is named. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium, which widens the margin of error around every metric above.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 20

- Refinancing risk is back-ended but concentrated. USD 500 million falls due in 2029 and USD 1,466 million in 2031, 74.57% of principal in the later year, and the book value of marketable debt exceeded fair value by USD 48 million at June 27, 2026, down from USD 136 million at March 28, 2026. The narrowing gap suggests debt is trading better, yet repayment slowed to USD 2 million in the third quarter, so the 2031 maturity will need market access rather than internal cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-03-28_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C09; calculation C10

- Overall the business profile is average and the cash-flow profile weak. The top risk is a raw-material cost spike or customer loss that cuts adjusted EBITDA toward the lowest recent quarterly run-rate of USD 336 million, which would lift debt to 5.66x and cash interest to 36.90% of earnings before any liquidity stress.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is momentum: third-quarter adjusted EBITDA rose 8.79%, the price-cost spread turned positive by USD 11 million, debt fell by USD 65 million in nine months, the issuer kept its free cash flow outlook and the discount on marketable debt narrowed sharply. These facts support a stable-to-improving direction and would justify a better view if the fourth quarter delivered the USD 58 million to USD 78 million of free cash flow the outlook implies and interest cover could be shown to be rising on a cash basis. The view would worsen if the third-quarter cash outflow of USD 28 million repeated, if the price-cost spread turned negative again as in the Americas in fiscal 2025, if remediation of the control weaknesses stalled, or if debt were raised to fund an acquisition.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; calculation C08; calculation C12
### Limitations

- Revolver availability net of letters of credit and any borrowing-base limit is not measured, so the liquidity conclusion could move from workable to tight if usable capacity is well below the USD 350 million commitment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1)
- Cash interest paid is known only for fiscal 2025, so the interest-cover conclusion cannot yet be shown to be improving or worsening on a cash basis.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Reported EBITDA is calculated by Financial foundation because the issuer states none, so the 7.60x reported multiple depends on that definition; a definition that also deducted other expense, net would lower EBITDA and raise the multiple slightly.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
- No rating or market price is supplied, so the refinancing conclusion rests on the filing's fair-value disclosure for debt; a market-based view could differ.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; Source readiness (CP-0)
- Covenants of the revolver and any intercreditor terms are not described, so the finding of no financial maintenance covenants covers only the term loan and secured notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. First, there is no debt maturity before October 2029 and no financial maintenance covenant on the term loan and secured notes, so default before 2029 would need a sharp earnings fall rather than a covenant trip. Second, liquidity of USD 630 million, cash plus the undrawn revolver, equals 33.14% of debt and is the main cushion against a near-term cash shortfall. Third, deleveraging is under way: debt repayments of USD 65 million and trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million lowered adjusted leverage from 5.51x to 5.11x. Fourth, the business spans two regions, 45 plants and more than 1,000 customers, so no single plant or region carries the whole credit. Fifth, the price-cost spread turned positive by USD 11 million in the third quarter, showing that pass-through can work.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C07

Weaknesses. First, net cash interest of USD 124 million took 35.03% of fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA and reported cover was 1.70x, so a small earnings fall removes cover. Second, free cash flow is thin: USD 32 million in nine months against an outlook of USD 90 million to USD 110 million, with a third-quarter outflow of USD 28 million. Third, the gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA is USD 122 million, 32.80% of adjusted earnings, so leverage is 7.60x if add-backs are not credited. Fourth, the top ten customers hold about 42% of sales and many have no long-term arrangement, while resin and pulp costs pass through only with a lag. Fifth, internal controls are not effective and ownership is not disclosed.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C12

### Company description

Magnera makes specialty nonwoven and film materials for hygiene, wipes, healthcare, apparel, filtration and food and beverage customers, from 45 plants split between the Americas, 57.21% of fiscal 2025 net sales, and the Rest of World, 42.79%. Personal Care was 48% and Consumer Solutions 52% of fiscal 2025 net sales, and consumer demand gives steadier volume than industrial end markets. The credit consequence is limited by two facts: organic volume still fell 2% in fiscal 2025, and the top ten customers are about 42% of net sales with no long-term arrangement for many of them, so revenue visibility is order flow rather than contract. That supports debt service in the near term but does not underwrite a refinancing on its own.

### Ownership and group structure

Magnera is a listed company created on November 4, 2024 when Treasure Holdco, a Berry subsidiary, merged with Glatfelter; pre-merger Treasure holders received 90% and Glatfelter holders kept 10%. No sponsor, current holder, board right or fee is disclosed, and the financing paid USD 1,111 million of cash to Berry at closing, 71.40% of the borrowing proceeds. Subsidiary guarantors support the secured notes but are not named, and no restricted-group or non-guarantor figures are given, so structural subordination is not established. The distribution is a historical one-off; since closing the company repaid debt, shows no further distribution and states an intent to pursue acquisitions, so the financial-policy risk is Medium rather than low.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Reported sales move with raw-material prices more than with volume, so sales are not a margin measure. In the first nine months of fiscal 2026 net sales rose 3.38% to USD 2,445 million, helped by USD 105 million of foreign currency and USD 112 million of merger revenue, and held back by a USD 117 million cut in selling prices and a 1% organic volume decline. In the third quarter volume turned positive at 1% and sales rose 2.15%. Pricing power is limited: costs pass through contractually only over time, at renewals and by other means, and customers can switch suppliers. Revenue is therefore recurring in demand, concentrated in buyers, cyclical in price and exposed to share loss to competitors including Ahlstrom, Avgol, Mativ, PFNonwovens, Freudenberg and Fitesa.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Cost of goods sold was 89.48% of fiscal 2025 net sales, leaving a gross margin of 10.52%, and selling, general and administrative cost 5.93%, so each 1% of net sales lost to unrecovered cost removes USD 33 million, about 8.83% of trailing adjusted EBITDA. The gross margin improved to 13.07% in the third quarter as the price-cost spread gained USD 11 million, helped by Project CORE and merger synergies. Raw materials are polymer resin, wood-based fibers and pulps, and energy and labour inflation also matter, but the fixed and variable cost split is not disclosed, so operating leverage cannot be measured. Margins can be defended only while pass-through works, which it did not in the Americas in fiscal 2025 when the price-cost spread cost USD 14 million.

### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital spending of USD 67 million in fiscal 2025 was 2.09% of net sales and about one third of depreciation and amortization of USD 206 million, and the outlook cuts fiscal 2026 spending to USD 60 million from USD 80 million. Net property, plant and equipment fell from USD 1,476 million to USD 1,393 million, so the asset base is shrinking and capex flexibility is partly a deferral that could reverse. Cash conversion is low: trailing operating cash flow of USD 172 million is 46.24% of trailing adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow of USD 113 million is 30.38%, after cash interest of USD 124 million, cash taxes of USD 22 million and USD 61 million of restructuring in nine months. Working capital helped, using USD 34 million in nine months against USD 119 million a year earlier, but receivable programs of unknown size may flatter operating cash flow.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry is high because named competitors include Ahlstrom, Avgol, Mativ, PFNonwovens, Freudenberg and Fitesa and competition is on price, service, quality and delivery, so unrecovered cost cannot be passed on easily and margin is exposed. Buyer power is high because the top ten customers hold about 42% of sales and many have no long-term arrangement, so volume and price are renegotiated at renewal and earnings can step down. Supplier power is moderate to high because resin and pulp prices are set outside the company and pass through with a lag, which makes cash conversion volatile. The threat of new entrants is moderate because plants, technology and customer qualification need capital, and the threat of substitutes is not established by the documents read.

### Macro and policy factors

Tariffs, inflation and currency are material enough to affect cash flow. Management cites changing tariffs and sanctions, inflation and market softness in its outlook. Sales are 43.63% in the United States and Canada and 56.37% elsewhere, and translation exposure to the euro, British pound, Argentine peso and Brazilian real moves reported sales and debt service, partly hedged by cross-currency swaps. The credit consequence is volatility in reported leverage and a pass-through test for tariffs, not a separate default driver.

### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are the 2029 maturity floor, USD 630 million of liquidity, falling adjusted leverage and regional diversification; weaknesses are thin cover, low cash conversion, the reported-to-adjusted gap and customer concentration. Opportunities that could raise credit quality are full delivery of Project CORE and merger savings, a fourth quarter that meets the free cash flow outlook, and remediation of the control weaknesses. Threats that could lower it are a raw-material spike without pass-through, a European volume decline, tariff escalation and a debt-funded acquisition.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

For the next twelve to twenty-four months the issuer's fiscal 2026 outlook is Adjusted EBITDA at the lower end of its range of USD 380 million to USD 410 million, operating cash flow of USD 150 million to USD 170 million, capital spending of USD 60 million and free cash flow of USD 90 million to USD 110 million. With nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 282 million the low end implies USD 98 million in the fourth quarter, level with the third quarter, and the free cash flow range implies USD 58 million to USD 78 million, which is a large step from a third-quarter outflow of USD 28 million. Tailwinds are the price-cost spread gain, a 1% organic volume gain in the third quarter, currency translation and Project CORE; headwinds are weak European volume, tariffs, raw-material inflation that management called a significant spike, restructuring cash and interest cost. Over three to five years the 2029 and 2031 maturities, the euro swap maturities in November 2027 and November 2029, and thin goodwill cushions of 6.71% and 7.88% at the last test dominate; an impairment would be non-cash but would signal weaker expected earnings.

### Downside scenario

The scenario starts with a raw-material cost spike that is passed on late while European volume stays soft, as in fiscal 2025 when organic volume fell 2% and the Americas price-cost spread cost USD 14 million. The first operating break is a negative price-cost spread, which cuts adjusted EBITDA; an illustrative case uses the lowest reported quarter, USD 84 million, annualised to USD 336 million, USD 36 million or 9.68% below the trailing figure; that quarter included Glatfelter only from November 4, 2024, so the case is harsher than a like-for-like trough. Debt of USD 1,901 million would be 5.66x that EBITDA and cash interest of USD 124 million would take 36.90% of it, and free cash flow would fall from USD 113 million to about USD 77 million before any tax effect. Management levers are cutting capital spending, which already fell by USD 20 million, ending restructuring spend and stopping prepayments; liquidity of USD 630 million and the absence of maturities before 2029 mean resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis in the window, but refinancing the 2029 notes at that earnings level would be harder and costlier. The observable triggers are a negative price-cost spread, organic volume turning negative again and a fourth-quarter free cash flow below USD 58 million.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Magnera presents an average business profile supported by regional and end-market diversification, 45 plants and no debt maturity before 2029, but credit quality is constrained by thin cash cover, the USD 122 million gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA, customer concentration and a weak control environment. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was USD 32 million in nine months and negative in the third quarter. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth and market access for USD 1,966 million of principal due in 2029 and 2031. The primary downside path is a raw-material cost spike passed on late, cutting adjusted EBITDA toward the lowest quarterly run-rate. Further analysis would require revolver availability, interim cash interest, receivable-program balances, the proxy statement and the executed debt documents. Top risk: thin cash cover on a debt load that must be refinanced in 2029 and 2031.

- The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA and the 7.60x multiple rest on a calculated definition. Severity Medium.
- No ratings, market prices or peer figures are supplied, so refinancing capacity and relative position are judged from the filings only. Severity Medium.
- The proxy statement and executed debt documents are not supplied, so ownership, consent rights, restricted-payment capacity and covenant terms of the revolver are not established. Severity Medium.
